restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r7-prefix-v1 only (seven partial rounds 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

time_log2 is the worst-case operation count of the algorithm of proof.md section 4 (at most K = 2 centres, every trial charged in full with the root isolation at its cap of 64 rounds, one thread), plus the offline bound of 1,000,000 operations of proof.md section 6.2, which is declared as preprocessing_log2 = 20 and is inside time_log2 (one quantity); memory_log2_bytes is the compacted 1.80 GB footprint (1,793,337,548 bytes <= 2^30.74) achieved via dynamic row streaming of modulus g and Barrett reciprocal MU and in-place folding modulo X^{N'} - 1 directly into the low half of buffer Y. Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2: every field operation, load, store, control operation and random word is priced 1/C, C = 216 + 21 r = 363.

success_probability 0.43348 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh independent uniform 256-bit random words (the cost model's random-word primitive) for the fixed target, derived from the one score-critical premise H-GEOM-w2 as 1 - (1 - q)^K - K (eps_coin + eps_iso) with q = 0.24733 (proof.md section 9.2).

heuristics.statement: Notation: p is the Pallas prime, D = 5^13, F in F_p[X] the fixed digest polynomial of proof.md section 2.3 at r = 7 (degree D). G(c,t) = (F(c+t) - F(c-t))/(2t) in F_p[c,t] (total degree D-1; G(c,t) = g_c(t^2) for the odd part g_c of proof.md section 3). k(c) is the number of nonzero squares S = t^2 with G(c,t) = 0 (k(c) = deg G_c). V is the Zariski closure of {(c,s1,s2) : G(c,s1) = G(c,s2) = 0, s1^2 != s2^2}. Premise: the plane curve G = 0 has at least one absolutely irreducible component defined over F_p, and V is a curve (pure dimension 1) with at most w = 2 absolutely irreducible components defined over F_p. Reduction (proved from Weil's bound with explicit constants, Bezout and the plane genus bound; proof.md section 9.2, numbers recomputed in Appendix D): for c uniform in F_p, E[k] >= 1/2 - e1 and E[k(k-1)] <= w/4 + e2 with e1 < 4.379e-21 and e2 < 0.00326265; Cauchy-Schwarz gives P(k >= 1) >= 0.2491869895 and Markov on k(k-1) gives P(k > 16) <= 0.0018502303, so the event 1 <= k <= 16 has probability at least q = 0.24733 for a uniform centre; two independent coin centres then succeed with probability at least 0.433487871 (with the coin and isolation terms of proof.md 9.2 and 9.4).
heuristics.scope: The fixed Poseidon target poseidon-orchard-r7-prefix-v1, this line construction (the line j = 0 of the first two rounds, odd part about a centre, proof.md sections 2-3), the polynomial F of proof.md section 2.3; centres uniform on F_p. Not claimed for other round counts. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic apart from the supporting heuristic H1-charging-rules: the Weil-Cauchy-Schwarz reduction, the isolation lemma (proof.md 9.4) and the independence of the centres (each draw uses fresh random words) are proved in proof.md.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the two moments of k(c) that H-GEOM-w2 gives through Weil's bound to the success of the algorithm at r = 7. The bound is explicit and applies for r <= 7 (at r >= 8 the plane genus bound exceeds the main term). Support: usable roots appeared at three of the four centres tried in our executed full-scale runs at r = 3, 4, 5 (proof.md section 10.1); the organizer-run experiments lowbits-birthday and line-ladder-w6, -w8, -w10, -w12 on the digest of the target and on the antipodal pairs of its line construction (proof.md section 10.2); the exact computations of Grok job 135 for the toy permutation on a generic line over the Pallas field (Theorem A: the hypothesis with w = 1 at one full round; Theorem B: absolute irreducibility of G = 0, a reduced pair scheme of pure dimension 1 and an absolutely irreducible off-diagonal u-scheme at two full rounds; Theorem D: degree exactly 5^N), and of Grok job 136 for the first N = 1, 2, 3, 4 full rounds of the Orchard parameter tuple on a generic line, re-run on the deployed constants and the attack line: (a) and (b) hold at N = 1, ..., 4, w = 1 at N = 1, the monodromy is S_m at N = 2, 3 (proof.md section 10.3), with the density of our line (proof.md section 10.3). Under (a) and 2-transitivity of the monodromy of H, w is 1 or 2 (Grok job 137, lemma: with the arithmetic monodromy Gamma inside the hyperoctahedral group B_m, K = Gamma meet F_2^m is one of 0, <1>, E, F_2^m once pi(Gamma) contains A_m, and w = 1 exactly when K contains the even-weight subspace E, w = 2 otherwise; the witnesses of Grok job 136 establish the hypotheses). Measured on the deployed Orchard constants and the attack's own line (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, using the Frobenius cycle types of H(c, u) and their lifts to G(c, t) = H(c, t^2) over F_p): N = 1 gives K = F_2^2 and w = 1; N = 2 (m = 12) gives K = F_2^12 and w = 1, witnessed by the 12-cycle specialisations c = 8 (two 12-cycles on G, omega = 0) and c = 24 (one 24-cycle, omega = 1) and the even permutation c = 6; N = 3 (m = 62) gives K = F_2^62 and w = 1, witnessed by the 62-cycle specialisations c = 82 (omega = 0) and c = 102 (omega = 1) and the even permutation c = 1. So w = 1 at N = 1, 2, 3 on the deployed constants, a measured trend, and the premise states w <= 2 at N = 13, which the lemma bounds by 2 given (a) and 2-transitivity.
heuristics.limitations: It concerns this F, not every polynomial of degree D: it is false for permutation polynomials (every pure composition of maps x -> a x^5 + b, p = 2 mod 5, is bijective and has k = 0), and a statement about components over the algebraic closure alone does not imply it (X^3 over F_101: two conjugate lines, no off-diagonal rational point). The explicit constants apply for r <= 7.

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 are the operation counts of the algorithm of proof.md section 4 under the stated rules: 1 per field operation (a Montgomery conversion is one multiplication), 1 per element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit, 1 per other executed index or control operation, 363 per reduced permutation evaluation, 31 per coin draw (one random 256-bit word), the allocator charged per executed operation, and a register file of 18 words of 256 bits per transform block as the only register assumption. The algorithm runs on one thread; there is no dispatch. Two further statements are declared: (A1) the Euclidean sequences of stage D are normal (every quotient has degree 1), which is the case the stage D count describes; (A2) the arena of proof.md section 7 (1,788,021,568 bytes) suffices for the largest trial under dynamic row streaming and in-place remainder folding.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the algorithm of proof.md section 4 at the target dimensions (m = 610,351,562, 1,610,612,736 evaluations of the line and transforms of 805,306,368 points), at their worst case over coins and data (proof.md section 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: The worst-case counts are derived by formula (proof.md section 6) and compared with the instrumented totals of our executed runs at smaller r (proof.md section 6.1). The arena rule (1.177 times the heap peak of the allocation walk plus 704 bytes) held at r = 3, 4, 5. A1 is measured on the digest family itself: in every run on the sibling targets with 0 and 1 partial rounds (same constants and line) all quotients of the Euclidean sequence of (g_c, S^((p-1)/2) - 1) had degree 1 (proof.md section 10.5). The stages at r = 7 need about 1.80 GB and 7.2e14 operations and are not hosted by the organizer sandbox (128 MiB, 20 s), so A1 and A2 at r = 7 are our theory: a vanishing leading coefficient in a remainder has probability about m/p < 2^-224, and the arena rule is the one that held at r = 3, 4, 5.
heuristics.limitations: Word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, bandwidth) are not part of the model.
